title: Navigating the Dutch Student Housing Crisis: Room.nl, Cooperatives & Living Costs

runs.t: Finding accommodation is one of the most important pre-departure tasks for international students in the Netherlands. The national Study in NL guidance warns that the country has a severe student-housing shortage and advises students to arrange housing before arrival. An admission offer is not a housing offer. Students should ask their institution about its housing allocation process, begin searching early and avoid transferring money before verifying the room and landlord.

Start with your university’s international office and housing service, then search recognised student-housing providers and private platforms in parallel. ROOM.nl, DUWO and SSH are useful names to investigate, but availability, eligibility, registration duration, allocation rules and city coverage differ. Budget using a range rather than assuming one national rent figure.

sections.title: Understand the shortage before accepting an offer

runs.t: Dutch students commonly live in shared student houses across the city rather than in large on-campus residences. Some institutions reserve a limited number of rooms for international students, often for a fixed period and subject to early application. Not every admitted student can receive institution-arranged housing. Ask in writing whether a room is guaranteed, what the deadline is, what the total rent includes and what happens after the initial contract ends.

runs.t: Study in NL publishes a list of housing platforms but explicitly says the list is not exhaustive and that it does not verify the reliability or quality of every provider. Treat a directory listing as a starting point for research—not an endorsement or guarantee.

sections.title: How to search effectively from India

runs.t: As soon as you accept an offer, email the university’s housing office and ask for its international-student housing procedure and deadlines.
Register with relevant platforms early. Check whether registration time or waiting-list position affects your chances.
Search beyond the city centre. Compare public transport, cycling distance, travel time and total monthly cost.
Prepare a short, credible introduction for landlords: programme, institution, arrival date, intended rental period and ability to provide the requested documents.
Arrange a live video viewing. Ask the person showing the room to demonstrate the address, room, shared areas and access.
Read the full contract before paying. Confirm whether utilities, internet, service costs and municipal charges are included.
Keep a temporary-arrival plan only if it is realistic and lawful; do not fly without a confirmed place to stay and a contingency plan.

sections.title: Housing scams: warning signs and safeguards

runs.t: A landlord claims to be abroad and refuses a live viewing or verifiable representative.
You are pressured to transfer a deposit immediately because “many people are waiting”.
The rent is unusually low for the location and room type, or the photos appear copied.
The landlord refuses to provide a written contract, proof of ownership/authority or a verifiable address.
Payment is requested through an unusual channel, cash without receipt, cryptocurrency or an account unrelated to the landlord/agency.
The listing says you can register at the address, but the landlord later says municipal registration is not possible. Clarify registration before signing.

The Study in NL advice is clear: do not sign a tenancy contract without having seen the room; arrange an online viewing and make sure you can clearly see the person you are speaking to. Be cautious about brokerage fees and do not pay rent in cash without a receipt.

sections.title: What should an Indian student budget?

runs.t: Study in NL gives a broad student living-cost estimate of €1,000–€1,500 per month. It lists room rent at roughly €450–€1,000 per month, depending on city, accommodation type and what is included. Amsterdam is generally more expensive than smaller university towns. These are planning ranges, not a quote or a guarantee of availability.

rows.t: Approximately €450–€1,000 per month for a room; city and contract inclusions matter.
Approximately €1,000–€1,500 per month as a broad student estimate.
Study in NL lists a Nibud 2024 average of €244 per month; use as a historical reference, not a 2026 guaranteed cost.
Cycling can reduce daily transport costs; include train/bus journeys and any commute to campus.
Check whether gas, electricity, water, internet and service costs are included in the advertised rent.
Allow for deposit, advance rent, bedding, kitchen items, bicycle, local registration and travel to campus.

runs.t: For tuition, Study in NL lists average non-EU/EEA fees of €9,000–€20,000 per year for Bachelor’s programmes and €12,000–€30,000 for Master’s programmes. These are averages only; use the exact programme fee for the intended academic year.
Confirm the legal name and contact details of the landlord or housing provider.
Check the address, room number, start/end dates, notice period and whether the contract is a tenancy or another occupancy arrangement.
Confirm whether municipal registration (BRP) at the address is allowed and required.
Check deposit amount, refund conditions, inventory and documented room condition.
Separate base rent from service charges and utilities; ask how annual reconciliations are handled.
Keep signed copies, payment records, messages and the move-in inspection report.

Use the official housing page of the student’s admitted institution.

faq.q: When should I start looking for student housing in the Netherlands?

runs.t: As soon as you apply or receive an offer—ideally before the admission decision if the institution permits it. Housing is scarce and some university allocations have strict deadlines.
Not necessarily. Some institutions offer a limited number of rooms or partner-provider places. Ask whether your specific place is guaranteed and what conditions apply.

faq.q: Is ROOM.nl only for Dutch students?

runs.t: Eligibility and access depend on the participating housing provider and the student’s circumstances. Check current registration and allocation rules directly on ROOM.nl and with the provider.

faq.q: How much is student rent in the Netherlands?

runs.t: Study in NL gives a broad range of €450–€1,000 per month for a room. The city, room type, bills and contract terms make a substantial difference.

faq.q: Can I pay a deposit before seeing the room?

runs.t: Avoid doing so unless you have independently verified the landlord, property, contract and payment route. Use a live viewing and keep a written record.
